openQuestions: TC-faithful by default on Windows and Linux (option 2), or a preset (option 3)?
Drop the mechanical Ctrl+↑ = Go to parent (TC uses Ctrl+↑ for "open folder in new tab"), and give Alt+↑ to Go to parent by taking it off Go to first item (Home stays)?
Add a Quit command off macOS? Linux convention is Ctrl+Q; Windows relies on Alt+F4. (Ctrl+Q is also TC's quick view.)

Linux: accept that Alt+F5 (compress), Alt+F2 (right volume), Alt+F7 (search) are dead on stock GNOME, with second keys only where proposed (Ctrl+Shift+F1/F2 for the volume choosers)? Or pick a second key for compress too?
AltGr on Windows: fix in the matcher (skip the physical-key fallback when `getModifierState("AltGraph")`), or move the Multi-rename option keys off Ctrl+Alt+letter?

Turn WebView2 browser accelerator keys off for every window (needs the Windows `with_webview` controller call, since Tauri 2.12.5 has no setter)? This also decides whether F5/Ctrl+R/Ctrl+P are safe in Settings and the viewer.
Keep F2 = Rename (Explorer and current Cmdr) rather than TC's F2 = reread? The proposal keeps it.
Add TC's Ctrl+I (switch to target pane) and Ctrl+< (root on European keyboards)?
Numpad vocabulary: name numpad keys distinctly (for example `Num+`) so Ctrl+Num + / Ctrl+Num - can be select all / deselect all without colliding with zoom?
Error screen's details toggle off macOS: Ctrl+Shift+D OK?
Windows `tab.next/prev`: keep Ctrl+Alt+→/← (works except on some Intel drivers, unverified) or drop it like Linux for one shared keymap?
Search dialog: its ⌘N / ⌘H / ⌘1–9 are unreachable off macOS today (Super combos); move them into the registry so they map like everything else?
